text:
Marathon Petroleum ticked up less than 1% today, but the real story is the 18% surge over two weeks—driven by a sharp spike in global oil prices and refinery demand. Brent crude climbed above $106 after a deadly Saudi airport attack, and U.S. refineries are running at 92.7% capacity, near full tilt. The gap between global oil ($125/barrel) and U.S. oil ($96/barrel) has also widened, which improves margins for refiners that process global crude; combined with tight diesel inventories and talk of easing sanctions on Russian fuel, the refining environment has tightened considerably in just two weeks.

The geopolitical moves—Trump's "energy ceasefire" with Russia, potential U.S. military involvement against Houthis, and the Saudi attack itself—have created an unusually volatile supply backdrop. For a major refiner, this kind of chaos typically lifts profitability, though the longer-term impact of Trump's Russia diesel deal and whether it actually brings relief to U.S. energy markets remains unclear.
